title: REFLECTing SPERET: Measuring and Promoting Ethics and Privacy Reflexivity in Eye-Tracking Research
benchmark_measurement: The paper develops two instruments, REFLECT (a qualitative questionnaire) and SPERET (a quantitative psychometric scale), to measure and promote privacy and ethics reflexivity among eye-tracking researchers. It does not measure any aspects of faith or religion.
findings: The paper has no findings related to religion. Its key findings are that eye-tracking researchers are highly attuned to privacy issues, less critically reflective about the limits of generalisability of their research, and show varied engagement with the broader social consequences of their work. The paper also found a gap in anticipatory ethics between basic and applied researchers.
references: 2015. Indicators for Promoting and Monitoring Responsible Research and Innovation: Report from the Expert Group on Policy Indicators for Responsible Research and Innovation. Publications Office of the European Union.
